verdict.rationale: LM Studio runs entirely on the user's own hardware. It also ships llmster, a documented headless daemon for servers, cloud instances and CI, which can serve OpenAI-like endpoints on the network. Community users confirm the headless flow works in real tools. Missing for 10: source-available or open-source code (community notes it is closed source), clear licensing for work and commercial self-hosted use (community reports terms prohibit work use), and in-depth deployment documentation for server installs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: llmster is the headless version of LM Studio, no desktop app required. It's ideal for servers, CI environments, or any machine where you don't need a GUI.
llmster is LM Studio's headless daemon for servers, cloud instances, and CI.
Serve local models on OpenAI-like endpoints, locally and on the network
The headless LM Studio flow is especially nice because it makes local inference usable from real tools instead of as a demo.
